message:
## Vulnerability Digest

Three relevant security reports and one version-specific possible match were identified in the last 24 hours. The highest-priority items are the Node.js/Brotli memory-corruption issue and the Ubuntu BIND exposure.

**Scope:** `Products.txt` and `List_of_SIA_Completed.txt` only, combined and deduplicated. `DLL_software_component.txt` was not read or combined.

**Scan window:** 2026-10-22 23:40 UTC through 2026-10-23 23:40 UTC (2026-10-23 05:10 IST through 2026-10-24 05:10 IST).

### Node.js security vulnerabilities

- **Affected product:** Node.js
- **Issues:** CVE-2026-105482, CVE-2026-105483, CVE-2026-106069, and CVE-2026-111497
- **Severity:** High according to Node.js. The Google CNA rates CVE-2026-111497 Critical, CVSS 4.0 score 9.2.
- **Description:** The fresh government alert covers DNS-name truncation, two TLS hostname-verification bypasses, and a bundled Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write. Crafted Brotli input can corrupt memory and may cause a crash, disclose memory, or permit remote code execution.
- **Why relevant:** The assigned SIA list contains Node.js 22.2.0 and 24.13.0. The vendor's fixed releases are 22.23.4, 24.22.1, and 26.12.1, so both listed versions fall below the corresponding fixed releases. CVE-2026-105483 affects 24.x/26.x; the other highlighted high-severity issues include 22.x where stated by the vendor.
- **Freshness note:** National cyber authorities published alerts on 23 October; CVE-2026-111497 was updated on 23 October. The underlying Node.js security release was issued on 21 October.
- **Sources:** [Node.js security release](https://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability/october-2026-security-releases), [Cyber Security Agency of Singapore alert](https://www.csa.gov.sg/alerts-and-advisories/alerts/al-2026-154/), [CVE-2026-111497 record data](https://app.opencve.io/cve/CVE-2026-111497)

### MongoDB Server and official drivers

- **Affected products:** MongoDB Server, MongoDB PHP Driver, MongoDB Go Driver, and libmongocrypt
- **Issues:** CVE-2026-112368, CVE-2026-104005, CVE-2026-96299, CVE-2026-104004, CVE-2026-107325, CVE-2026-107324, and CVE-2026-106433
- **Severity:** Medium according to CERT-In; CERT-In separately describes a high risk of denial of service, memory corruption, and information disclosure.
- **Description:** The report covers BSON-decoding recursion and length-validation weaknesses, missing authorization checks, collection-validator handling errors, integer overflow, and memory-management issues.
- **Why relevant:** MongoDB is explicitly monitored, including Community Server and MongoDB Shell entries. CERT-In names Server 8.0 before 8.0.34, 8.3 before 8.3.13, and 9.0 before 9.0.4, plus specified PHP Driver, Go Driver, and libmongocrypt versions. The exact SIA-listed Community Server 7.0.9 and Shell 2.2.6 are not named in these affected ranges, so confirm whether other MongoDB server or driver deployments exist.
- **Source:** [CERT-In CIVN-2026-0520, issued 23 October 2026](https://www.cert-in.org.in/s2cMainServlet?VLCODE=CIVN-2026-0520&pageid=PUBVLNOTES01), [MongoDB security alerts](https://www.mongodb.com/resources/products/alerts)

### Ubuntu BIND package

- **Affected product:** Ubuntu `bind9`
- **Issue:** CVE-2026-94300
- **Severity:** Medium priority according to Ubuntu; CVSS 3.1 score 8.1 / Important in other vendor scoring.
- **Description:** Replayed GSS-TSIG-signed UDP messages, combined with crafted queries to an attacker-controlled zone, can corrupt memory in the `named` process and may permit remote code execution.
- **Why relevant:** Ubuntu is monitored, and Canonical marks `bind9` vulnerable on maintained Ubuntu releases from 18.04 through 26.10. CERT-In's 23 October BIND report also covers three denial-of-service CVEs, but this digest retains only CVE-2026-94300 because its Ubuntu mapping was directly verified.
- **Sources:** [Ubuntu CVE-2026-94300 status](https://ubuntu.com/security/CVE-2026-94300), [CERT-In CIVN-2026-0519](https://www.cert-in.org.in/s2cMainServlet?VLCODE=CIVN-2026-0519&pageid=PUBVLNOTES01)

### Possible match needing review

**LiteLLM 1.107.0 supply-chain compromise:** CERT-In reported credential theft and remote-code-execution behavior in the LiteLLM 1.107.0 PyPI release and related container images. The assigned SIA list specifies LiteLLM 1.83.10, which is outside the reported affected version; verify that no environment drifted to or cached 1.107.0. No CVE or formal severity rating was stated in the advisory. [CERT-In CIAD-2026-0053](https://www.cert-in.org.in/s2cMainServlet?VLCODE=CIAD-2026-0053&pageid=PUBVLNOTES02)

### MongoDB ecosystem verification

The dedicated sweep checked MongoDB Server Community and Enterprise, `mongod`, `mongos`, Atlas and Atlas services, Ops Manager, Cloud Manager, Compass, `mongosh`, Database Tools, Kubernetes Operator, drivers, connectors, BI Connector, Charts, Realm/App Services, official integrations, maintained libraries, MongoDB-owned notices, CVE/NVD records, GitHub advisories, CISA sources, and credible security reporting. The CERT-In MongoDB report above was the only in-window match; no additional fresh Atlas, management, client-tool, or service advisory was verified.

### Review priority

Immediate review is recommended for the listed Node.js 22.x/24.x installations and Ubuntu systems running BIND. Inventory MongoDB Server/driver versions before treating the grouped MongoDB advisory as applicable, and verify that LiteLLM remains on the approved 1.83.10 release.
